standards.name: JSON Schema
standards.fact: The official specification page identifies Draft 2020-12 as the current published JSON Schema version.
standards.use: Machine-readable schemas for catalogs, manifests, records at external/data boundaries.
standards.prune: Do not turn every internal Python object into JSON Schema; use it where machine-readable contracts add value.

standards.name: Agent Skills
standards.fact: A Skill is a directory centered on SKILL.md with progressive disclosure; OpenAI documents compatibility with the open Agent Skills standard.
standards.use: Reusable on-demand procedures, not mutable factual catalogs or global instructions.
standards.prune: Avoid giant always-on AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md instruction databases.

standards.name: Model Context Protocol
standards.fact: The 2026-07-28 MCP core is stateless, uses JSON-RPC 2.0, and defines tools/resources/prompts plus opt-in extensions such as Tasks and Skills.
standards.use: Agent-to-tool/data/context integration when a real MCP boundary exists.
standards.prune: Do not model the application's internal architecture as MCP.

standards.name: Agent2Agent (A2A) Protocol
standards.fact: Official A2A documentation identifies 1.0.0 as the latest released version and positions A2A as an interoperability protocol for independent agents.
standards.prune: Do not use A2A for local in-process or CLI-internal boundaries.

standards.name: OpenAPI Specification
standards.fact: OpenAPI 3.2.1 is the latest published OpenAPI specification as reviewed on 2026-10-01.
standards.use: Machine-readable HTTP API contract only when a public HTTP API exists.
standards.prune: Do not add an HTTP service merely to justify OpenAPI.

standards.name: AsyncAPI Specification
standards.fact: AsyncAPI 3.1.0 describes message-driven APIs in a protocol-agnostic machine-readable form.
standards.prune: Do not add AsyncAPI for an internal SQLite append log.

standards.name: CloudEvents
standards.fact: The CloudEvents repository identifies v1.0.2 as the stable released core specification while main contains work in progress.
standards.use: Cross-system event envelope when interoperability is actually required.
standards.prune: Do not wrap every internal domain record in CloudEvents.

standards.name: OpenTelemetry Semantic Conventions
standards.fact: OpenTelemetry semantic conventions provide common trace/metric/log/resource names and the current specification page is marked Development.
standards.use: Exporter/bridge for observability, never the application's authoritative schema.
standards.prune: Keep internal observation contracts stable and map to OTel at the edge.

standards.name: CycloneDX
standards.fact: CycloneDX 1.7 is the current published CycloneDX specification in the reviewed official documentation.
standards.use: SBOM generation when the build/release platform does not already provide an equivalent artifact.
standards.prune: Prefer CI/package-manager generated SBOMs over hand-maintained BOM files.

standards.name: Sigstore Cosign
standards.fact: Cosign is Sigstore's recommended CLI for artifact signing and verification.
standards.use: Release artifact signing/verification if the distribution channel benefits from it.
standards.prune: Prefer platform-native trusted publishing/attestations first; do not add bespoke key infrastructure.

standards.name: OpenAI Agents API
standards.fact: The Agents API models Agent, Environment, Session, and Events/items and supports continuing or steering durable sessions.
standards.prune: Do not copy its session/task model into PeerHub Core.

standards.name: OpenAI Agents SDK
standards.fact: The Agents SDK provides code-first agent runtime patterns with tools and context across steps.
standards.prune: Use only when the project needs a code-owned harness; do not add by default.

standards.name: Claude Managed Agents
standards.fact: Claude Managed Agents separates Agent, Environment, Session and Events, and Agent definitions can include tools, MCP servers and Skills.
standards.prune: Keep vendor Agent/system-prompt configuration outside PeerHub Core.

standards.name: Microsoft Agent Framework / Harness Agent
standards.fact: Agent Framework distinguishes Agents, Harness Agents, Workflows and Integrations; Harness adds long-task scaffolding such as context compaction, memory, file access and observability.
standards.prune: Do not recreate every harness capability inside PeerHub.

standards.name: Google ADK / agents-cli
standards.fact: Google's agent tooling supports Skills and a broader build/evaluate/deploy/observe workflow around agent projects.
standards.use: Reference for agent development, eval, deployment and Skill workflows.
standards.prune: Do not depend on ADK unless it becomes a real runtime target.
